target.description: Resolve Hans J. Nissen's Uruk and I as the A01 documentation and find-context control, preserve its testimonial genre and rights boundary, and derive a source-first architecture for distinguishing excavation-time observations, missing records, later inferences, and explicit reconstructions without importing the article body.
required_properties: exact article identity, author, publication date, serial identifier, and publisher route
article-text rights distinguished from artifact-image and linked-material rights
memoir and eyewitness-testimony genre distinguished from neutral excavation documentation
official and classical excavation, stratigraphy, metadata, and provenance controls
established scholarship on context required for archaeological data reuse
freshest direct work on provenance, legacy-data semantics, and bounded reconstruction
acceptable_substitutions: official publisher HTML plus PDF route for exact Work identity without acquiring either payload
current official archaeology ontologies and repository guidance for field-record architecture
publisher metadata and abstracts for comparison literature when full text is not needed

results.rationale: A1 models documented progressive recording and matter removal while requiring excavation-time material state to remain distinct from later causal interpretation. AP11, AP13, and AP13.2 distinguish physical evidence, inferred stratigraphic relation, and justification.

snapshot.reason: The versioned official specification remains the canonical reference; no ontology payload is imported.

results.rationale: The guidance treats documentation, metadata, formats, preservation, access, reuse, and intellectual-property boundaries as lifecycle concerns rather than post-hoc cleanup.

snapshot.reason: The live official guidance route is retained as a dated architectural control.

results.rationale: The established stratigraphic-sequence method is a classical control for ordering documented relations. It cannot recover observations that were never made or records that were lost.

snapshot.reason: No book payload is needed for the bounded architectural conclusion.

channels.source_name: Springer Nature, CNR, MDPI, and Cambridge University Press current literature
channels.exact_query: Find the freshest directly relevant 2024-2026 work on archaeological provenience and archival provenance, semantic legacy-data integration, cross-format field recording, and transparent reconstruction of incomplete context.

results.title_as_displayed: Kindred contexts: archives, archaeology, and the concept of provenance

declared_rights.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, with separately credited third-party material exceptions.

results.rationale: The article distinguishes archaeological provenience or findspot from archival provenance and emphasizes that relationships and documentation history condition meaning and interpretation.

snapshot.reason: The publisher page supplies the required current conceptual and rights metadata.

results.title_as_displayed: Legacy data or just archaeological data?
results.rationale: The article directly warns that heterogeneous nonsemantic legacy data cannot be made analytically reliable by automation alone; substantial human interpretation and semantic curation remain necessary.

snapshot.reason: No full-text payload or license conclusion is needed for the bounded control.

results.title_as_displayed: Curating Archaeological Provenience Data Across Excavation Recording Formats
results.rationale: The current case directly concerns preserving provenance and provenience across plans, sections, photographs, finds, spatial fields, and changing excavation-record formats. Exact reuse terms remain unasserted in this planting.

snapshot.reason: Only exact metadata and methodological relevance are retained; no content or license claim is imported.

results.title_as_displayed: Old Data, New Horizons: 3D Modeling as a Catalyst for Recontextualizing Fragmentary Legacy Data
results.rationale: The freshest direct case demonstrates useful 3D-GIS recontextualization while retaining manual decisions, heterogeneous-record limits, non-equivalent layer labels, and explicit reconstruction boundaries.

snapshot.reason: No article or data payload is needed to establish the reconstruction-versus-observation control.
